newsitem.title: UK: Bottomley says no immediate plans to privatise C4.
newsitem.headline: Bottomley says no immediate plans to privatise C4.

text.p: Britain's National Heritage Secretary said on Thursday there were no immediate plans to privatise the Channel 4 television station.
Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley said in a BBC radio interview that all options would be considered but added privatisation of the channel was not "a matter (for action) at the moment".
"My concerns are that we should have a diversity of broadcasting in this country...that we should have a high standard in public service broadcasting," added Bottomley .

"We should continue to look at financial regimes for the BBC, for Channel 4, for the independent companies, but decisions will be made at appropriate times when we can be sure it will safeguard all the objectives of quality broadcasting."
Set up in 1982, Channel 4 is a non-profit making corporation with a programme remit requiring it to appeal to interests not covered by the mainstream ITV network.
The right-wing of the ruling Conservatives want the party to include a commitment to the privatisation of Channel 4 in the manifesto for the next general election, due by May 1997.
